sections.heading: 1. What is Friction
points: **Friction** = the force that **opposes the relative motion** between two surfaces in contact.
It acts in the direction **opposite** to motion.
Friction is caused by the **irregularities (roughness)** on the two surfaces interlocking — even 'smooth' surfaces have tiny bumps.

sections.heading: 2. Factors and Types
points: Friction depends on: how **rough** the surfaces are, and how hard they are **pressed together** (weight).
**Rougher surfaces → more friction**; smoother → less.

sub: **Sliding friction** — when one surface slides over another.
**Rolling friction** — when one body rolls over another (smallest).

points: **Rolling friction < sliding friction < static friction.**

sections.heading: 3. Friction: Friend and Foe
points: **Advantages:** lets us **walk, write, hold, grip and stop vehicles (brakes)**; without friction we could not move or hold anything.
**Disadvantages:** causes **wear and tear** and produces **heat** (energy loss).
**Increasing friction:** treaded shoe soles/tyres, grooves; **Decreasing friction:** **lubricants (oil, grease), polishing, ball bearings (convert sliding to rolling)**.

sections.heading: 4. Fluid Friction (Drag)
points: **Fluids (liquids/gases) also exert friction**, called **drag**, on objects moving through them.
Drag depends on the object's **speed, shape and the nature of the fluid**.
To reduce drag, bodies are given a **streamlined shape** (e.g. birds, fish, aeroplanes, boats).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Friction opposes relative motion; caused by surface irregularities.
Rougher/heavier → more friction; smoother → less.
Rolling friction < sliding friction < static friction.
Friction helps walking/writing/braking; but causes wear & heat.
Reduce friction: lubricants, ball bearings (sliding→rolling); fluid friction = drag → streamlined shape.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Order: **rolling < sliding < static** friction (rolling is the least).
**Ball bearings** reduce friction by converting **sliding into rolling**.
Friction is **necessary** — we cannot walk, write or brake without it.
Friction in fluids = **drag**, reduced by a **streamlined** shape.
